title: Which of the eight angles made by the diagonals are equal?
description: Both diagonals of a rectangle make eight small angles with the sides. They are measured with a protractor and sorted into two groups of four equal angles. Keeko's doubt is that all eight angles are equal.
teaching_notes: One idea: the eight angles that the diagonals make with the sides fall into two groups of four equal angles, and the angles at one corner add up to a right angle. Watch for students who think all eight angles are equal.

source: In rectangle PQRS, with both diagonals drawn, the eight angl
video_script.why: A learner measures the eight angles made by the diagonals of a rectangle and groups the equal ones.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle PQRS with both diagonals and the eight angles a, b, c, d, e, f, g and h
video_script.anchor: a rectangle PQRS with both diagonals drawn and the eight small angles named a to h
video_script.wrong_move: assumes every angle at a corner is the same size without measuring
video_script.payoff_line: The eight angles make two groups of four equal angles.

final_answer.value: d = e = a = h and c = f = g = b. Also c + d = 90 degrees
final_answer.spoken: two groups of four equal angles

maths_rules: angles next to the long sides PQ and SR: d, e, a and h, each about 34 degrees in a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle
angles next to the short sides PS and QR: c, f, g and b, each about 56 degrees
each corner of a rectangle is a right angle, so c + d = 90 degrees
the diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so the triangles they make are mirror images
video_script.design: The rectangle and its diagonals are drawn, the eight angles are measured, and the equal ones are grouped by the side they touch.
